title: Developing Drosophila melanogaster Models for Imaging and Optogenetic Control of Cardiac Function
protocol: Change the 3rd chromosome balancer TM3 Sb[1] to TM6 Sb Tb, creating w[1118]; P{y[+t7.7] w[+mC]=GMR88D05-GAL4}attP2/TM6 Sb Tb (Hand-GAL4/TM6 Sb Tb).
Set crosses in vials with regular cornmeal media.
Keep the genetic crosses in a 25 °C, 70% humidity incubator on specially formulated all-trans retinal (ATR)-containing media for 5 days for larvae collection and 6 days for pupae collection.
Combine five Hand-GAL4 /TM6 Sb Tb virgin females and two to three males from UAS-opsin stocks per vial.
Prepare ATR-containing media vials the next day.
Mix Semi-Defined Food according to BDSC26 instructions, using only sucrose (5.14 g/100 mL).
Cool the mixture to approximately 60 °C with constant stirring.
Dispose of fly food to narrow fly vials using a serological pipette, adding 5 mL per vial.
Vortex the contents at maximum speed for 10 seconds.
Plug the vials and wrap them in dark fabric to protect from light.
Let the vials dry for at least 12 hours (overnight).
Transfer flies steadily laying eggs to the vials with ATR-containing food.
Protect racks with vials from light exposure.
Discard parents after 24-48 hours to prevent over-population of the vial.
Collect non-Tb progeny and use them for heart imaging.
Pick UAS-opsin/Hand-GAL4 larva/pupa from the vial.
Place the picked larva/pupa on tissue.
Gently wipe off media from the body surface using a painting brush.
Prepare the microscope slide and place a small piece of double-sided tape in the middle.
Gently place the larva/pupa on the tape surface with the dorsal side up and perpendicular to the long side of the slide using a brush or fine tweezers.
Apply gentle pressure to attach the larva/pupa to the tape surface.
Set up the slide on the imaging stage, larva/pupa facing down.
Turn on the OCT light source by laser control software.
Open the custom-written SD-OCT control software and click on the Preview window.
Set the scan parameters in the SD-OCT software.
Use micromanipulators to control the sample stage to bring the fly heart into focus.
Adjust the focal position to minimize light reflection from the fly cuticle surface.
Consider applying mineral oil on the larva/pupa surface to minimize reflection.
Ensure that the fly heart can be fully viewed in the image window without any distortions, being blocked out by tissue, and non-negligible shadows and reflections.
Set scan parameters for M-mode OCT image acquisition.
Reduce number of A-scans compared to previous steps for faster frame rate.
Acquire five sets of control data without red light stimulation pulses.
Calculate resting heart rate from control experiment.
Design light pulse sequences in custom OCT control software.
Add designed light pulse sequences in "Settings" tab.
Set pulse frequency, width, and duration according to protocols.
Open light controller software from Table of Materials.
Choose Pulse Mode in "Mode Selection".
Double-click figure for "Pulse Profile" settings.
Select Follower Mode in Pulse Profile settings.
Keep OFF intensity as 0.
Set ON intensity percentage based on calculations.
Acquire M-mode videos of the beating Drosophila heart with light stimulation using OCT control software.
Repeat video acquisition measurements 5 times.
Open custom-developed fly heart segmentation software.
Select file for analysis in the GUI.
Enter vertical and horizontal boundaries of the heart region in pixels in top text boxes.
Click Resize to adjust view.
Ensure entire heart region is visible and fills box by adjusting boundaries if necessary.
Click Predict to select heart region in every slice, taking approximately 3 minutes.
Click HR Plot once prediction is completed.
Select correct peak or valley areas for analysis.
Choose Pulse and then HR to generate final figure.
Save functional parameters in .csv files.
